shows.name: US vintage live sale, numbered items one at a time plus a lettered $2 bargain bin (Trusty Huckster Mercantile)
shows.note: Host shows one item at a time and says '<price> by giving me number N'; viewers claim by typing the bare number and a moderator confirms '#N goes to <viewer>'. Catalogue (40 numbers, prices) recovered from host speech in the auto-captions, cross-checked against moderator confirmations. Item 56 is a mystery box sold as a guessing game: the host hides a number between 50 and 60 and the first viewer to type it wins, so bare numbers 50-60 typed around 0:12-0:14 are guesses, not claims of items 51, 52 or 54. 28, 42 and 77 found no takers; 17 and 54 drew 'no takers' first and sold later (17 claimed at about 1:36:39, while 51 was on screen); 77 was re-shown on request at about 1:26:39. 70 had two sets (qty 2); the second set was re-offered at about 1:46:38. From about 1:47:09 a $2 bargain bin uses letters as codes (Q, S, N, H, T, C, Y, F, K, R, M, G, shown in that order); the host says his letter tags got mixed up. Sale ends about 2:05:11. Timeline in eval/raw/heldout-v3/timelines.json.

shows.name: US Paparazzi $5 jewellery live sale, numbered pieces shown one at a time (Sparkle Seeds)
shows.note: YouTube backup stream (Facebook video failed). Every piece is $5. The host holds up a numbered card and says 'this is N'; viewers claim by typing the number, often with a colour or a part ('59 purple', '98 set', '151 necklace', '132 earring'). Catalogue of 64 numbers recovered from host speech in the auto-captions; speech-to-text garbles many numbers ('3:02'=302, '4:58'=458, 'for 71'=471, 'to 44'=244, 'one 5/8'=158, 'for 61'=461, '2:36'=236, 'for 83'=483, 'to 85'=285, 'for 97'=497, 'one 55'=155, '$4.99'=499, '1/4'=124, 'three-sixteen'=316, 'sixty six four six six'=466, 'one to 26'=126). Every number viewers typed is in the catalogue. 465 is only a confirmed claim, never described; 314 was said right after a silver-and-red side-hinge bracelet and nobody claimed it; 435 was read out from a comment and is omitted. Pieces sold as necklace/bracelet/earrings or a set cannot be encoded as variants, so they are one variant each and the part is in the title; colour variants exist only where the host named colours (281, 59, 22, 53, 385). Stock per number is not stated except 108 (three pieces, then a waiting list); other qty values are nominal. Re-shows on request are repeat timeline entries; current is null while the host catches up on comments.

shows.name: US comic book claim sale, lettered wall of slots A-W refilled through the show, claims and offers (Very Gary Comics)
shows.note: Channel's first live claim sale. Comics hang on a wall in lettered slots; viewers write 'claim <letter>' or make offers ('$300 for letter M', 'would you take 150 on U?'), and the owner posts payment requests. Books on a slot change after they sell, so items are slots, not titles. Slot letters A-W were heard in host speech in the auto-captions; O and U come through only as 'on oh' / 'on you' and are confirmed by viewers asking for grade and price on O and U. No X. Owner payment requests range from $34 to $1,900; priceCents is nominal. There is no item timeline (any slot can be claimed at any time), so current is null for every row.

shows.name: India suits, kurtis and dupatta sets live, one design at a time, Hindi/Hinglish (Honey Money Collection)
shows.note: Designs shown one at a time; viewers book in chat with size and colour ('book 40 for me', 'book black M', 'ek xl mera bhi', 'book 44 pink'). Prices vary by design (mostly ₹450-₹950, some ₹3500-₹5300); free shipping on two suits. Item '1' stands for the design on screen. Some designs come in letter sizes (the host lists small, medium, large, XL, double XL) and others in numeric sizes ('36 se 46'), so the size grid holds both. Colours are those the host names at least five times in the captions; any one design has only some of them. qty is nominal.

shows.name: India chikankari kurti live, one piece at a time, Hindi/Hinglish (ZAID CHIKAN WORLD)
shows.note: Kurtis shown one piece at a time, each a single size; most are ₹600; some heavier designs are priced higher (₹1050-₹4000 heard). Viewers book with size and colour ('book my 54 green', '48 me yellow', 'book for me purple tie and die'). The host gives the size as a number and names the letter size: 40 = L, 42 = XL, 44 = XXL, 46 = 3XL, 48 = 4XL, 50 = 5XL, 54 = 7XL. Item '1' stands for the piece on screen; the grid is the union of sizes (34-58) and of colours the host names at least five times. qty is nominal.

shows.name: India Xuping jewellery live (rings, bracelets, earrings, pendants), one piece at a time, Hindi/Hinglish (Simransethi)
shows.note: Pieces shown one at a time; prices vary (roughly ₹100-₹500). Viewers book by colour, ring size or price ('white for me no. 6', 'bk dark blue 7 no.', 'Book 185 silver matar chain', 'book 2.4 for me'). Item '1' stands for the piece on screen. Sizes are the ring numbers the host names (5-10; 'number 10' is asked for but not stocked for the first ring) and the bracelet sizes 2.4, 2.6 and 2.8; each colour also has a no-size variant for earrings, pendants and chains. Colours are the polish and stone colours the host names at least three times (dark/midnight blue folded into blue). qty is nominal.
